rules.statement: Don't set `GenerateDocumentationFile` to false in a test project; turn off only CS1591 there so the documentation file is still generated and IDE0005 (unused usings) runs in the build.
rules.why: IDE0005 only reports in the build when the documentation file is generated. Turning it off in a test project silently stops unused-using checks there.
rules.check: Look for `<GenerateDocumentationFile>false</GenerateDocumentationFile>` in test project files or test-only MSBuild blocks, and for docs that say test projects generate no documentation file.

rules.statement: In a test project, use `null!` only to pass a deliberate null to the code under test, as in an argument-validation test, and never to silence a nullable warning.
rules.why: Production code never uses the null-forgiving operator. Passing a deliberate null to test argument validation is the one exception the conventions allow.
rules.check: In test code, find each `!` null-forgiving use and confirm it is a `null!` argument that tests null handling, not a suppression on a dereference or assignment.

rules.statement: A NuGet publish workflow must fail when a packed package's version differs from the release tag's version or when nothing was packed, and must fail rather than report success when every package version is already on the feed.
rules.why: With `--skip-duplicate`, a run that pushed nothing, or pushed the wrong version because a project set its own `Version`, would otherwise look like a successful release.
rules.check: In publish workflows that run `dotnet nuget push`, look for a check that each `.nupkg` matches the tag version, a check that something was packed, and a check that fails when all packages already exist before writing a success summary.

rules.statement: Name the store-neutral exception for a lost optimistic-concurrency race `StoreConcurrencyException`, matching the name used across NCodeGroup repositories.
rules.why: Each NCode repository should give the same type the same name so the repositories stay consistent.
rules.check: Look for store-neutral concurrency-conflict exceptions with a different name, such as `ConcurrencyConflictException`, in code or decision records.
